attacks.title: SQL Injection via Username Parameter in Login Query
attacks.reason: The login query uses a parameterized statement with a placeholder (?) and passes the username as a separate parameter, preventing SQL injection regardless of input content.

attacks.title: Reflected XSS via Username in Error Responses
attacks.reason: The login endpoint returns generic error messages (e.g., 'Invalid credentials') and never reflects the username in JSON responses, eliminating the reflected XSS vector via error messages.

attacks.title: JWT Algorithm Confusion Attack (RS256 to HS256)
attacks.reason: The code only implements JWT token generation (HS256) but lacks any token verification logic; algorithm confusion attacks target verification, which is absent.

attacks.title: Missing Authentication on Password Reset / Account Recovery Endpoint
attacks.reason: The code does not implement any password reset or account recovery endpoints, so the attack vector (missing authentication on those endpoints) is entirely absent.

attacks.title: No SQL Injection vulnerability found
attacks.reason: All database queries use parameterized statements with placeholders, preventing SQL injection.

attacks.title: No Cross-Site Scripting vulnerability found
attacks.reason: The API exclusively returns JSON responses with Content-Type: application/json, performs no HTML rendering, and user-controlled data is only stored in structured logs or returned in JSON error messages, eliminating XSS vectors in the server-side code.

attacks.title: Hardcoded default JWT secret enables token forgery
attacks.reason: The JWT_SECRET defaults to a cryptographically random value generated at startup via os.urandom(32).hex(), not a static hardcoded string, preventing token forgery via known default secrets.

attacks.title: No missing authentication for critical function found
attacks.reason: The code only exposes public authentication endpoints (/login, /register) and contains no critical functions that require authentication, so CWE-306 is not applicable.
